summary: Specifies the frame format for sending IPv6 packets over Ethernet and how link-local addresses are formed there. It is on the standards track as a proposed standard. It was replaced by RFC 2464.

eli5.summary: It tells how to put IPv6 messages into the envelopes that Ethernet cables understand, and how to make a local address.

questions: how is ipv6 sent over ethernet
how are ipv6 link-local addresses formed
what is the ipv6 ethernet type code
subtitle: Sending IPv6 messages across Ethernet cables

tldr.problem: IPv6 is a new version of IP, but networks use Ethernet to physically send packets. The standard for connecting IPv6 to Ethernet was needed.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1972 specifies that IPv6 packets go into Ethernet frames with type code 86DD hexadecimal, and link-local addresses are formed from the Ethernet MAC address and a standard prefix.
tldr.outcome: It was replaced by RFC 2464, which provided equivalent functionality.

today: RFC 1972 was obsoleted by RFC 2464, which provides the standard method for IPv6 over Ethernet.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
IPv6 is the next version of the Internet Protocol, offering much larger address space than IPv4. RFC 1972 specifies how IPv6 packets are sent across Ethernet networks, including the frame format, the maximum transmission unit size, and how to form IPv6 addresses on Ethernet interfaces.

The document also specifies how IPv6 addresses are mapped to Ethernet addresses for both unicast (one-to-one) and multicast (one-to-many) communication, and defines the format of the Source/Target Link-layer Address options used in IPv6 Neighbor Discovery messages on Ethernet.
sections.eli5: This memo is the rulebook for putting IPv6 packets into Ethernet frames and creating temporary addresses that work on the local network.

sections.title: Frame Format and MTU Size
sections.content:
IPv6 packets are transmitted in standard Ethernet frames. The Ethernet header contains the source and destination Ethernet addresses and the type code, which must be set to 86DD hexadecimal to indicate IPv6. The data field contains the IPv6 header followed immediately by its payload, and may include padding octets to meet Ethernet minimum frame size.

The default maximum transmission unit (MTU) size for IPv6 packets on Ethernet is 1500 octets. This size can be reduced by a Router Advertisement containing an MTU option, or manually configured on each node. Larger MTU values in Router Advertisements must be ignored.
sections.eli5: IPv6 packets go in Ethernet envelopes with a special number saying what is inside. The packet can be up to 1500 bytes, but smaller sizes are allowed if the router says so.

sections.title: Address Mapping and Link-Local Addresses
sections.content:
Link-local addresses are formed by combining the standard 80-bit prefix FE80:0000:0000:0000 with the 48-bit IEEE 802 Ethernet address of the interface. This allows nodes to automatically create usable addresses for local network communication without central administration.

For unicast communication (sending to a single Ethernet address), the Source and Target Link-layer Address options in Neighbor Discovery messages contain the 48-bit Ethernet address. For multicast, IPv6 multicast addresses are mapped to Ethernet multicast addresses: the first two octets are 3333 hexadecimal, followed by the last four octets of the IPv6 multicast address.
sections.eli5: Computers create their own temporary addresses by mixing a special pattern with their Ethernet address. When sending to multiple computers at once, a special multicast address starting with 33 33 tells Ethernet which computers should hear the message.
